questions.question_description: Implement a Doubly Linked List supporting creation, insertion at the beginning, middle, and end, as well as displaying the list.
questions.input_format: Integer N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'ins_beg X', 'ins_mid pos X', 'ins_end X', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'display', print space-separated elements. Print 'Empty' if empty or 'Invalid' for bad insertions.
questions.hints: Maintain 'head' and 'tail' pointers to allow O(1) insertions at the end. For middle insertions, traverse to pos-1.

test_cases.input:
6
ins_beg 10
ins_beg 20
ins_mid 1 30
ins_end 40
ins_mid 5 50
display

questions.solution_explanation: A complete doubly-linked list focused on creation and insertion operations only (beginning, middle, and end).

questions.question_description: Implement a Doubly Linked List supporting creation, deletion at the beginning, middle, and end, as well as displaying the list.
questions.input_format: Integer N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'ins_end X', 'del_beg', 'del_mid pos', 'del_end', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'display', print space-separated elements. Print 'Empty' if empty or 'Underflow'/'Invalid' for bad deletions.
questions.hints: First generate a list using 'ins_end X'. For 'del_mid', carefully connect the previous node's next pointer to the next node, and vice versa.

questions.solution_explanation: A complete doubly-linked list focusing on deletion limits (beginning, middle, and end). It populates data utilizing a basic end-insertion.
